title: Deployment Marshall 1:1 Brief
body:
Purpose: prep notes for my 1:1 with the deployment marshall ahead of Wed readiness sync. This is a working scratchpad — short bullets, questions I want to surface, and the small checklist we'll run through live.

Context: Rollout v2.14 -> targeted public canary (10%) then ramp 3 stages to 100% over 48h if metrics stable. Major changes: kernel selector tweak for long-context, updated KV cache hot-path, new quantization fallback for T4 pools. Known risk: memory growth in canary around seq len > 4096 observed in infra QA (INF-3245).

Topline talking points for 1:1:
- Quick state: health & infra capacity (are we green to start canary tomorrow 09:00 PT?)
- Risk spotlight: memory regression on long sequences — scope (only T4?), mitigation in place?
- Canary plan: traffic slices, duration, primary metrics to watch, escalation triggers
- Rollback & fallback: who executes, where to route traffic on fail, communication timeline
- Ops staffing: on-call + rotation coverage for first 24h ramp
- Post-canary eval gating: pass/fail criteria and who signs off

Notes to self / things to confirm with Marshall:
- Confirm that infra has reserved burst capacity for canary -> ask Ben to confirm nodes are pinned.
- Confirm the hotfix that limits KV cache growth is included in the canary build (PR #782).
- Verify monitoring alert thresholds are aligned with canary expectations (Maya owns dashboards).
- Get explicit rollback checklist: step 1 (pause new sessions), step 2 (drain existing), step 3 (route back to v2.13), step 4 (postmortem owner).

Go/No-Go quick matrix (for the call) — run through each and mark: must be yes to go
- Infra capacity: nodes reserved + autoscale tested -> YES?
- Canary image built & smoke tests green -> YES?
- Monitoring: dashboards and alerts wired into #deploy-ops -> YES?
- Rollback plan documented and rehearsed -> YES?
- Customer-facing comms drafted (status page blurb) -> YES?
- Legal/compliance check for private tenant churn -> N/A or YES?

Signals & SLOs to watch during canary (call out to marshall):
- 95th/99th latency for common routes (chat/generation) — regressions > 15% = trigger
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained for 5m = immediate pause
- Memory > baseline + 20% on any single node = investigate; if > 40% = pause
- Throughput drop > 10% correlated with latency = degrade and potentially rollback

Proposed staffing & timeslots:
- Canary start: 2026-03-13 09:00 PT.
- Primary watch: 09:00–15:00 PT (Asha + Ben + Maya onshift)
- Overnight watch: on-call rotation (Rafael backup)
- Post-canary review: 2026-03-14 11:00 PT

Open questions I need Marshall to answer in 1:1:
- Is the memory regression root-cause limited to a single kernel path or likely wider?
- If we hit the memory trigger during canary, do we auto-fallback to quantized variant or roll back to v2.13 image? Pros/cons?
- Can support teams (CS) be pre-briefed with templated CS response? Who will own that message?
- Any outstanding security review items for the private deploy customers?

Quick draft script for the canary start announcement (status page / internal):
"We are initiating a staged canary for v2.14 starting 2026-03-13 09:00 PT. Traffic will be routed incrementally. We will monitor latency, error rate, and memory for 48h. If thresholds breach, we will pause and roll back. Expected impact: none for 90% of users; up to 10% initially. For incidents, see #deploy-ops and status.redwood.ai."

Personal checkpoints after 1:1:
- Update runbook with any changes Marshall asks for (my TODO)
- Re-sync Maya on thresholds and confirm Grafana links
- Ping Ben for capacity confirmation and node pinning
- Draft support-facing blurb and drop in CS review thread

Tone + reminders for the call:
- Be concise — three bullets: capacity, risk, sign-off path
- I want a firm yes/no on memory root cause before we start
- Capture any deviation from the rollback plan as a separate action

Misc scratch (brainstorm / half-formed):
- Consider adding a 'degraded-fast-fail' policy: if latency spikes but error rates stay low, we pause ramp rather than rollback fully. Could reduce churn for transient network issues. Need to decide on thresholds.
- If memory growth only occurs with seq>4096, consider traffic filter to limit sequence length on canary for first stage. Might be less clean but buys time.

End of notes. Will pare down into agenda bullets before the 1:1 and attach to the meeting invite.
go_no_go_checklist: Canary build includes KV cache fix (PR 782)
Rollback plan documented and owner assigned
action_items: Asha: Update runbook with rollback steps + assign postmortem owner (due 2026-03-12)
Ben: Confirm node pinning and reserved capacity for canary (INF-3245) (due 2026-03-12)
Maya: Validate alert thresholds and hand over Grafana links (due 2026-03-12)
Rafael: Standby as overnight backup and review oncall rota (due 2026-03-12)
Asha: Draft status page and CS template and post to #customer-success for review (due 2026-03-12)
